title: Spiritual Tourism in Rajasthan: Pushkar, Ajmer, Nathdwara and Jain Temples
seoTitle: Spiritual Places in Rajasthan: Pushkar, Ajmer & More | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a spiritual trip in Rajasthan: Pushkar and Ajmer Sharif, Nathdwara and Eklingji, Ranakpur and Dilwara, Khatu Shyam Ji and Karni Mata, with routes.
description: A guide to spiritual tourism in Rajasthan: Pushkar's lake and Brahma temple, the dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer, Shrinathji at Nathdwara and Eklingji near Udaipur, the Jain temples of Ranakpur and Dilwara, Khatu Shyam Ji, Salasar Balaji, Karni Mata and Galtaji, festivals, routes and seasons.
dek: Rajasthan's sacred sites range from a desert lake town and a great Sufi shrine to some of India's finest Jain temples.

hero.alt: White temples and ghats on the shore of Pushkar Lake, Rajasthan

intro: Rajasthan is best known for forts and palaces, but it is also a major pilgrimage state. Pushkar, with its sacred lake and one of the very few temples to Brahma, sits 15 km from Ajmer, home to the dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Near Udaipur are Shrinathji at Nathdwara and the Eklingji temple, and in the Aravalli hills stand the Jain temples of Ranakpur and Dilwara.
In the Shekhawati region, Khatu Shyam Ji and Salasar Balaji draw huge crowds, and Karni Mata near Bikaner is famous for the rats revered in its courtyard.
quickAnswer: Rajasthan's main spiritual destinations are Pushkar (the lake, ghats and Brahma temple), the Ajmer Sharif dargah, Shrinathji at Nathdwara and Eklingji near Udaipur, the Jain temples of Ranakpur and Dilwara at Mount Abu, Khatu Shyam Ji and Salasar Balaji in Shekhawati, and Karni Mata near Bikaner. October to March is the best time; the Pushkar fair falls in the month of Kartik.
takeaways: Pushkar and Ajmer are 15 km apart and easily combined.
Nathdwara and Eklingji are near Udaipur; Ranakpur is about 90 km away.
Dilwara's Jain temples are at Mount Abu.
Khatu Shyam Ji and Salasar Balaji are among Rajasthan's busiest temples.
October to March is best; summers are very hot.

items.name: Pushkar
body: Fifty-two ghats around the lake, the Brahma temple and the Savitri temple on a hill; the Pushkar fair falls in Kartik (October or November).

image.caption: Brahma temple, Pushkar

items.name: Ajmer Sharif
body: The dargah reached through the old bazaar; the Urs falls in the month of Rajab.

items.name: Nathdwara and Eklingji
body: Shrinathji is worshipped in the Pushtimarg tradition, with darshan at set times through the day; Eklingji is about 25 km from Udaipur.

items.name: Ranakpur and Dilwara
body: Two of India's finest groups of Jain marble temples.

sections.heading: More sacred places
list: Salasar Balaji, a Hanuman temple in Churu district.
Galtaji near Jaipur, with temples and sacred tanks in a gorge.
Ramdevra near Pokaran, the shrine of Baba Ramdev, revered by Hindus and Muslims.

sections.heading: Where to stay
list: Pushkar: guesthouses and small hotels by the lake; the town is vegetarian and alcohol is not served near the ghats.
Ajmer: hotels near the dargah for early visits, or stay in Pushkar.
Udaipur: the best base for Nathdwara, Eklingji and Ranakpur.
Mount Abu: hill-station hotels near Nakki Lake for Dilwara.

sections.heading: Etiquette notes
list: Pushkar's ghats are sacred: remove shoes, do not photograph people bathing, and decline pushy offers of 'free' puja.
Cover your head at Ajmer Sharif; caps and scarves are sold nearby.
At Nathdwara, darshan happens at set times (jhankis) through the day; plan around them.
At Karni Mata, walk carefully; the rats are revered, and seeing a white one is considered lucky.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly and follow each place of worship's rules on dress, phones and photography.
Carry water and sun protection; Rajasthan's heat is intense from April to June.
Follow Jain temple rules on leather and food at Ranakpur and Dilwara.
packing: Light cotton clothing and a shawl for winter nights
